source.text: Ἐγένοντο δὲ καὶ ψευδοπροφῆται ἐν τῷ λαῷ, ὡς καὶ ἐν ὑμῖν ἔσονται ψευδοδιδάσκαλοι, οἵτινες παρεισάξουσιν αἱρέσεις ἀπωλείας, καὶ τὸν ἀγοράσαντα αὐτοὺς δεσπότην ἀρνούμενοι, ἐπάγοντες ἑαυτοῖς ταχινὴν ἀπώλειαν·

records.literal_gloss: There were but also false prophets among the people, as also among you there will be false teachers, who will bring in alongside heresies of destruction, even the [one] having bought them Master denying, bringing upon themselves swift destruction;

en.L: But there were also false prophets among the people, just as among you also there will be false teachers, who will slip in heresies of destruction, even denying the Master who bought them, bringing swift destruction on themselves.
en.B: In the past there were false prophets among the people of Israel, and in the same way there will be false teachers among you. They will quietly bring in teachings that lead to destruction, and they will even disown the Master who bought them. So they will bring swift destruction on themselves.
en.R: Long ago, false prophets came among God's people Israel. In the same way, false teachers will come among you. Without anyone noticing, they will bring in false teachings that destroy people. They will even turn against the Master who paid the price to make them {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own. So they will soon bring destruction on themselves.

es.L: Pero hubo también falsos profetas en el pueblo, como también entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} habrá falsos maestros, que introducirán a escondidas herejías de destrucción, llegando a negar al Amo que los compró, y atrayendo sobre sí mismos una destrucción rápida.
es.B: En el pasado hubo falsos profetas en el pueblo de Israel, y del mismo modo habrá falsos maestros entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Introducirán con disimulo enseñanzas que llevan a la destrucción, y hasta renegarán del Amo que los compró. Así atraerán sobre sí mismos una destrucción rápida.
es.R: Hace mucho tiempo aparecieron falsos profetas en Israel, el pueblo de Dios. Del mismo modo, aparecerán falsos maestros entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Sin que nadie lo note, traerán enseñanzas falsas que destruyen a la gente. Hasta se volverán contra el Amo que pagó el precio para hacerlos {{deity_pronoun:suyos|Suyos}}. Por eso pronto se traerán la destrucción a sí mismos.

sw.L: Lakini walikuwako pia manabii wa uongo miongoni mwa watu, kama vile miongoni mwenu pia watakuwako walimu wa uongo, ambao wataingiza kwa siri uzushi wa maangamizi, hata wakimkana Bwana aliyewanunua, wakijiletea wenyewe maangamizi ya haraka.
sw.B: Zamani walikuwako manabii wa uongo miongoni mwa watu wa Israeli, na vivyo hivyo watakuwako walimu wa uongo miongoni mwenu. Wataingiza kimyakimya mafundisho yanayoleta maangamizi, na hata watamkana Bwana aliyewanunua. Hivyo watajiletea maangamizi ya haraka.
sw.R: Zamani sana, manabii wa uongo walitokea katikati ya Israeli, watu wa Mungu. Vivyo hivyo, walimu wa uongo watatokea katikati yenu. Bila mtu yeyote kutambua, wataleta mafundisho ya uongo yanayoangamiza watu. Hata watamgeuka Bwana aliyelipa gharama ili wawe mali {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Kwa hiyo hivi karibuni watajiletea maangamizi.

decisions.choice: the people: Israel, among whom false prophets arose in the past
decisions.reason: τῷ λαῷ is the usual name for Israel as God's people. The Law warns against prophets who lead the people astray (Deuteronomy 13:1-5), and the prophets met many who spoke lies in God's name (Jeremiah 23:9-32; Ezekiel 13). Peter has just spoken of the true prophets (1:19-21); now he sets the false ones beside them.

decisions.choice: they will bring in, alongside the truth and without being noticed, teachings that divide and lead to destruction
decisions.reason: παρεισάξουσιν means to bring something in beside what is already there, usually quietly. αἱρέσεις first meant a chosen opinion, or the group that held it (Acts 5:17; 24:5), and then the divisions such opinions cause (1 Corinthians 11:19; Galatians 5:20). Here it is the teaching that splits a church, and ἀπωλείας says where it leads. Destruction (ἀπώλεια) comes three times in verses 1-3.

decisions.choice: the Master who bought them: Christ, pictured as an owner who has paid for his slaves
alternatives: God, as in Deuteronomy 32:6, where God is the Father who acquired his people
decisions.reason: δεσπότην is the word for a slave's owner. Buying (ἀγοράσαντα) is the language of the slave market, which the New Testament uses for Christ's purchase of his people (1 Corinthians 6:20; 7:23; Revelation 5:9). Jude 4, the parallel verse, names "our only Master and Lord, Jesus Christ". To deny him is to disown the one they belong to; the text says he bought them, and still they deny him.

decisions.choice: a parallel to Jude 4
decisions.reason: Jude 4 speaks of people who slipped in unnoticed and deny the only Master. 2 Peter 2 and Jude share much of their material and often their order: compare 2:1-3 with Jude 4, 2:4 with Jude 6, 2:6 with Jude 7, 2:10-12 with Jude 8-10, 2:13 with Jude 12, 2:15 with Jude 11, 2:17 with Jude 12-13 and 2:18 with Jude 16.

decisions.choice: the people of Israel (B); God's people Israel (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the people (m1), which a reader of this letter would not otherwise know.

decisions.choice: heresies of destruction (L); teachings that lead to destruction (B); false teachings that destroy people (R)
decisions.reason: In current English "heresy" names a doctrine the church has formally judged false. Literal keeps the word; Balanced and Readable say what Peter means by it: teaching that divides and ruins (m2).

decisions.choice: the Master who paid the price to make them his own
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of buying a slave (m3).

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms
decisions.reason: Peter writes to the churches in the plural. As in the rest of the New Testament, each plural "you" and its verb is a reader setting: ustedes (the default) or vosotros.

decisions.choice: Amo
decisions.reason: "Señor" is kept for the Greek word for Lord. The word here is the owner of slaves, and Spanish "amo" is a slave's master, so it keeps the picture of an owner who bought them (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: Bwana aliyewanunua
decisions.reason: Swahili "bwana" is the ordinary word for a slave's master, so it keeps the picture of an owner who bought them (m3). It is also the word for "Lord"; that suits a verse whose parallel, Jude 4, calls the same person "our only Master and Lord". "Mmiliki" (owner) would sound like the owner of property, not a person's master.

decisions.choice: mali {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}
alternatives: a span for every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in Swahili, the deity_pronoun setting goes only on free pronouns and possessives ("yake"); pronouns marked inside the verb ("aliyewanunua") cannot take a capital. Readable says "mali yake" (his property) for "his own", which keeps the picture of a slave bought by a master.

source.text: καὶ πολλοὶ ἐξακολουθήσουσιν αὐτῶν ταῖς ἀσελγείαις, δι’ οὓς ἡ ὁδὸς τῆς ἀληθείας βλασφημηθήσεται·

records.literal_gloss: And many will follow after their sensualities, because of whom the way of the truth will be blasphemed;

en.L: And many will follow their acts of sensuality, because of whom the way of the truth will be blasphemed.
en.B: Many people will follow their shameless ways, and because of them the way of truth will be slandered.
en.R: Many people will copy the shameless way these teachers live. Because of them, people will say evil things about the way of truth.

es.L: Y muchos seguirán sus desenfrenos, por causa de los cuales el camino de la verdad será blasfemado.
es.B: Mucha gente seguirá su conducta desvergonzada, y por causa de ellos el camino de la verdad será difamado.
es.R: Muchas personas imitarán la vida desvergonzada que llevan estos maestros. Por culpa de ellos, la gente dirá cosas malas del camino de la verdad.

sw.L: Na wengi watafuata matendo yao ya ukosefu wa haya, ambao kwa sababu yao njia ya kweli itakufuriwa.
sw.B: Watu wengi watafuata tabia zao zisizo na haya, na kwa sababu yao njia ya kweli itasemwa vibaya.
sw.R: Watu wengi wataiga jinsi walimu hao wanavyoishi bila haya. Kwa sababu yao, watu watasema mabaya juu ya njia ya kweli.

decisions.choice: sensuality: open, unrestrained indulgence, especially sexual, done without shame
decisions.reason: ἀσέλγεια is behavior that throws off all restraint and does not care who sees it (Romans 13:13; Galatians 5:19). The plural means acts or habits of it. The same word describes Sodom in verse 7 and the bait the false teachers use in verse 18.

decisions.choice: the way of truth: the Christian faith as a way of life
decisions.reason: "The way" is a name for the Christian faith in Acts (9:2; 24:14), and "the way of righteousness" in verse 21 says the same. It is a road one walks, not only a set of ideas. Its truth is the message the apostles handed on (1:12).

decisions.choice: blasphemed: spoken against by outsiders because of the believers' conduct
decisions.reason: βλασφημέω means to speak of someone or something with contempt. The thought echoes Isaiah 52:5, quoted in Romans 2:24: God's name is spoken against among the nations because of his people. Peter urges the opposite in 1 Peter 2:12.

decisions.choice: blasphemed (L); slandered (B); say evil things about (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek word. In current English "blaspheme" is used only of speech against God, so Balanced and Readable say "slander" and "say evil things" for speech against the Christian way (m3).

decisions.choice: matendo ya ukosefu wa haya (L); tabia zisizo na haya (B); bila haya (R)
decisions.reason: Shameless, unrestrained living, as in Galatians 5:19, where the same Greek word is "ukosefu wa haya". "Ufisadi" is the older word for it, but today it most often means corruption in public office, so it is not used at any level (also in 2:7 and 2:18). "Uasherati" would narrow it to sexual sin.

source.text: καὶ ἐν πλεονεξίᾳ πλαστοῖς λόγοις ὑμᾶς ἐμπορεύσονται· οἷς τὸ κρίμα ἔκπαλαι οὐκ ἀργεῖ, καὶ ἡ ἀπώλεια αὐτῶν οὐ νυστάζει.

records.literal_gloss: And in greed with made-up words you they will trade on; for whom the judgment from long ago not is idle, and the destruction of them not slumbers.

en.L: And in greed they will trade on you with made-up words; for them the judgment from long ago is not idle, and their destruction is not asleep.
en.B: In their greed they will make money out of you with stories they have invented. But the judgment passed on them long ago has not been sitting idle, and their destruction has not fallen asleep.
en.R: These teachers are greedy, and they will make up stories to get money from you. But God's judgment on them was decided long ago, and it is not sitting still. Their destruction is not asleep.

es.L: Y por avaricia harán de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} mercancía con palabras inventadas; para ellos el juicio de hace mucho tiempo no está ocioso, y su destrucción no dormita.
es.B: En su avaricia sacarán dinero de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} con historias que ellos mismos han inventado. Pero el juicio dictado contra ellos hace mucho tiempo no ha estado ocioso, y su destrucción no se ha quedado dormida.
es.R: Estos maestros son codiciosos, y van a inventar historias para sacar{{plural_you:les|os}} dinero. Pero el juicio de Dios contra ellos se decidió hace mucho tiempo, y no está quieto. Su destrucción no está dormida.

sw.L: Na kwa uchoyo watawafanya ninyi bidhaa kwa maneno ya kubuni; kwao hukumu ya tangu zamani haikai bure, na maangamizi yao hayasinzii.
sw.B: Kwa uchoyo wao watajipatia fedha kutoka kwenu kwa hadithi walizozibuni wenyewe. Lakini hukumu iliyotolewa juu yao zamani haijakaa bure, na maangamizi yao hayajalala usingizi.
sw.R: Walimu hao ni wachoyo, na watabuni hadithi ili wapate fedha kutoka kwenu. Lakini Mungu aliamua hukumu yao zamani, nayo haijatulia. Maangamizi yao hayajalala.

decisions.choice: they will trade on you: use you for profit, as goods to be sold
decisions.reason: ἐμπορεύομαι means to do business or to trade in something. Used with a person as its object, it means treating people as merchandise. Greed (πλεονεξίᾳ) comes again in verse 14.

decisions.choice: made-up words: stories they have invented
decisions.reason: πλαστός means formed or molded, as a potter shapes clay, and so made up. Peter has said that he and the apostles did not follow invented stories (1:16); the false teachers do the very thing they will accuse the apostles of.

decisions.choice: the judgment is not idle and the destruction is not asleep: their punishment, decided long ago, is already on its way
decisions.reason: The judgment and the destruction are pictured as servants that are awake and at work, not lying idle or dozing. ἔκπαλαι ("from long ago") points to the judgment already shown in Scripture, which verses 4-8 go on to recall; Jude 4 also speaks of people "long ago written down for this judgment". The picture answers the scoffers of 3:4, who say nothing ever changes.

decisions.choice: God's judgment on them was decided long ago
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the judge, which the passive picture implies (verses 4 and 9).

source.text: Εἰ γὰρ ὁ θεὸς ἀγγέλων ἁμαρτησάντων οὐκ ἐφείσατο, ἀλλὰ σειραῖς ζόφου ταρταρώσας παρέδωκεν εἰς κρίσιν τηρουμένους, καὶ ἀρχαίου κόσμου οὐκ ἐφείσατο, ἀλλὰ ὄγδοον Νῶε δικαιοσύνης κήρυκα ἐφύλαξεν, κατακλυσμὸν κόσμῳ ἀσεβῶν ἐπάξας, καὶ πόλεις Σοδόμων καὶ Γομόρρας τεφρώσας καταστροφῇ κατέκρινεν, ὑπόδειγμα μελλόντων ἀσεβέσιν τεθεικώς, καὶ δίκαιον Λὼτ καταπονούμενον ὑπὸ τῆς τῶν ἀθέσμων ἐν ἀσελγείᾳ ἀναστροφῆς ἐρρύσατο βλέμματι γὰρ καὶ ἀκοῇ ὁ δίκαιος ἐγκατοικῶν ἐν αὐτοῖς ἡμέραν ἐξ ἡμέρας ψυχὴν δικαίαν ἀνόμοις ἔργοις ἐβασάνιζεν οἶδεν κύριος εὐσεβεῖς ἐκ πειρασμοῦ ῥύεσθαι, ἀδίκους δὲ εἰς ἡμέραν κρίσεως κολαζομένους τηρεῖν, μάλιστα δὲ τοὺς ὀπίσω σαρκὸς ἐν ἐπιθυμίᾳ μιασμοῦ πορευομένους καὶ κυριότητος καταφρονοῦντας.

records.literal_gloss: For if the God angels having sinned not spared, but with chains of gloom having cast into Tartarus handed [them] over for judgment being kept, \v 5 and [the] ancient world not spared, but eighth Noah of righteousness herald guarded, a flood on [the] world of ungodly [ones] having brought, \v 6 and cities of Sodom and Gomorrah having reduced to ashes to overthrow condemned, an example of [things] coming for ungodly [ones] having set, \v 7 and righteous Lot being worn down by the of the lawless in sensuality conduct rescued, \v 8 for by seeing and hearing the righteous [one] dwelling among them day from day [his] righteous soul with lawless deeds was tormenting, \v 9 knows [the] Lord godly [ones] out of trial to rescue, but unrighteous [ones] for [the] day of judgment being punished to keep, \v 10 especially but those after flesh in desire of defilement going and lordship despising.

en.L: For if God did not spare angels who had sinned, but, casting [them] into Tartarus, handed [them] over to chains of gloom, being kept for judgment, \v 5 and did not spare the ancient world, but guarded Noah, the eighth, a herald of righteousness, when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought a flood on the world of the ungodly, \v 6 and, reducing the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah to ashes, condemned [them] to overthrow, having set [them as] an example of what is coming for the ungodly, \v 7 and rescued righteous Lot, worn down by the conduct of the lawless in [their] sensuality \v 8 (for by what he saw and heard, that righteous [man], living among them, tormented [his] righteous soul day after day with [their] lawless deeds), \v 9 [then] the Lord knows how to rescue the godly out of trial, and to keep the unrighteous under punishment for the day of judgment, \v 10 and especially those who go after the flesh in defiling desire and despise lordship.
en.B: God did not spare the angels who sinned. He threw them down into Tartarus and handed them over to chains of deepest darkness, where they are held for judgment. \v 5 Nor did {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spare the ancient world. When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought the flood on a world of ungodly people, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} kept Noah safe with seven others, Noah who proclaimed righteousness. \v 6 He condemned the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah to ruin and burned them to ashes, and made them an example of what is coming to the ungodly. \v 7 But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rescued Lot, a righteous man who was worn down by the shameless conduct of lawless people. \v 8 Living among them day after day, that righteous man tormented his righteous soul over the lawless deeds he saw and heard. \v 9 If God did all this, then clearly the Lord knows how to rescue those who are godly from their trials, and how to hold the unrighteous under punishment until the day of judgment, \v 10 above all those who chase after the flesh with its defiling desires and who look down on the Lord's authority.
en.R: God did not let the angels who sinned go free. He threw them down into Tartarus, the deepest prison, and put them in chains in the dark. There they are being held until the time of judgment. \v 5 God did not spare the people of the ancient world either. He sent a flood on that world, which was full of people who did not honor {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} kept Noah safe, along with seven others. Noah was the one who told people about righteousness. \v 6 God also judged the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah. He burned them until only ashes were left. In this way {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} showed what will happen to people who do not honor {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \v 7 But God rescued Lot, a righteous man. Lot was deeply troubled by the shameless way the wicked people around him lived. \v 8 Day after day this righteous man lived among them, and the evil things he saw and heard hurt him deep inside. \v 9 So you can be sure of this: the Lord knows how to rescue people who honor {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} when they go through hard times. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} knows how to keep wicked people under punishment until the day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} judges them. \v 10 This is true above all for those who chase after the evil desires of the body that make them unclean, and who look down on the Lord's authority.

es.L: Porque si Dios no perdonó a ángeles que habían pecado, sino que, arrojándolos al Tártaro, los entregó a cadenas de oscuridad, guardados para el juicio, \v 5 y no perdonó al mundo antiguo, sino que guardó a Noé, el octavo, heraldo de justicia, cuando trajo un diluvio sobre el mundo de los impíos, \v 6 y, reduciendo a cenizas las ciudades de Sodoma y Gomorra, [las] condenó a la ruina, poniéndolas [como] ejemplo de lo que vendrá para los impíos, \v 7 y rescató al justo Lot, abrumado por la conducta de los inicuos en [su] desenfreno \v 8 (porque por lo que veía y oía, aquel justo, viviendo entre ellos, atormentaba día tras día [su] alma justa con [sus] obras inicuas), \v 9 [entonces] el Señor sabe rescatar de la prueba a los piadosos, y guardar a los injustos bajo castigo para el día del juicio, \v 10 y sobre todo a los que andan tras la carne en deseo que contamina y desprecian el señorío.
es.B: Dios no perdonó a los ángeles que pecaron. Los arrojó al Tártaro y los entregó a cadenas de profunda oscuridad, donde están guardados para el juicio. \v 5 Tampoco perdonó al mundo antiguo. Cuando trajo el diluvio sobre un mundo de gente impía, protegió a Noé junto con otras siete personas, a Noé, que proclamaba la justicia. \v 6 Condenó a la ruina las ciudades de Sodoma y Gomorra, las redujo a cenizas y las puso como ejemplo de lo que les espera a los impíos. \v 7 Pero rescató a Lot, un hombre justo que estaba agobiado por la conducta desvergonzada de gente sin ley. \v 8 Aquel justo, que vivía entre ellos, atormentaba día tras día su alma justa por las obras inicuas que veía y oía. \v 9 Si Dios hizo todo esto, es claro que el Señor sabe rescatar de sus pruebas a los piadosos, y mantener a los injustos bajo castigo hasta el día del juicio, \v 10 sobre todo a los que corren tras la carne con sus deseos que contaminan, y que desprecian la autoridad del Señor.
es.R: Dios no dejó libres a los ángeles que pecaron. Los arrojó al Tártaro, la prisión más profunda, y los encadenó en la oscuridad. Allí están guardados hasta el tiempo del juicio. \v 5 Dios tampoco perdonó a la gente del mundo antiguo. Envió un diluvio sobre aquel mundo, que estaba lleno de gente que no {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} honraba. Pero protegió a Noé y a otras siete personas. Noé era el que le hablaba a la gente acerca de la justicia. \v 6 Dios también juzgó a las ciudades de Sodoma y Gomorra. Las quemó hasta que solo quedaron cenizas. Así mostró lo que les pasará a los que no {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} honran. \v 7 Pero Dios rescató a Lot, un hombre justo. A Lot le dolía mucho la vida desvergonzada que llevaba la gente malvada a su alrededor. \v 8 Día tras día este hombre justo vivía entre ellos, y las maldades que veía y oía lo herían en lo más hondo. \v 9 Así que {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} estar seguros de esto: el Señor sabe rescatar a los que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} honran cuando pasan por momentos difíciles. Y sabe mantener a los malvados bajo castigo hasta el día en que los juzgue. \v 10 Esto vale sobre todo para los que corren tras los malos deseos del cuerpo que los hacen impuros, y que desprecian la autoridad del Señor.

sw.L: Kwa maana ikiwa Mungu hakuwahurumia malaika waliotenda dhambi, bali, akiwatupa katika Tartaro, aliwakabidhi kwa minyororo ya giza, wakilindwa kwa ajili ya hukumu, \v 5 wala hakuuhurumia ulimwengu wa kale, bali alimlinda Nuhu, wa nane, mtangazaji wa haki, alipoleta gharika juu ya ulimwengu wa wasiomcha Mungu, \v 6 na, akiiteketeza miji ya Sodoma na Gomora hadi kuwa majivu, aliihukumu iangamizwe, akiiweka [iwe] mfano wa yale yatakayowajia wasiomcha Mungu, \v 7 na alimwokoa Lutu mwenye haki, aliyechoshwa sana na mwenendo wa wasio na sheria katika ukosefu [wao] wa haya \v 8 (kwa maana kwa yale aliyoyaona na kuyasikia, mtu yule mwenye haki, akiishi kati yao, aliitesa siku kwa siku nafsi [yake] yenye haki kwa matendo [yao] yasiyofuata sheria), \v 9 [basi] Bwana anajua kuwaokoa watauwa kutoka katika majaribu, na kuwaweka wadhalimu chini ya adhabu kwa ajili ya siku ya hukumu, \v 10 na hasa wale wanaofuata mwili katika tamaa ya unajisi na wanaodharau ubwana.
sw.B: Mungu hakuwahurumia malaika waliotenda dhambi. Aliwatupa chini katika Tartaro, akawakabidhi kwa minyororo ya giza nene, ambako wanalindwa mpaka hukumu. \v 5 Wala hakuuhurumia ulimwengu wa kale. Alipoleta gharika juu ya ulimwengu wa watu wasiomcha Mungu, alimlinda Nuhu pamoja na watu wengine saba, Nuhu aliyetangaza haki. \v 6 Aliihukumu miji ya Sodoma na Gomora iangamizwe, akaiteketeza hadi ikawa majivu, akaifanya kuwa mfano wa yale yatakayowapata wasiomcha Mungu. \v 7 Lakini alimwokoa Lutu, mtu mwenye haki aliyekuwa amechoshwa sana na mwenendo usio na haya wa watu wasiojali sheria. \v 8 Kwa kuwa aliishi kati yao siku baada ya siku, mtu huyo mwenye haki aliitesa nafsi yake yenye haki kwa sababu ya matendo maovu aliyoyaona na kuyasikia. \v 9 Ikiwa Mungu alifanya hayo yote, ni wazi kwamba Bwana anajua jinsi ya kuwaokoa watauwa kutoka katika majaribu yao, na jinsi ya kuwaweka wadhalimu chini ya adhabu mpaka siku ya hukumu, \v 10 hasa wale wanaofuata tamaa za mwili zinazonajisi, na wanaodharau mamlaka ya Bwana.
sw.R: Mungu hakuwaacha huru malaika waliotenda dhambi. Aliwatupa chini katika Tartaro, gereza lililo chini kabisa, akawafunga kwa minyororo gizani. Huko wanalindwa mpaka wakati wa hukumu. \v 5 Mungu hakuwahurumia pia watu wa ulimwengu wa kale. Alileta gharika juu ya ulimwengu ule, uliokuwa umejaa watu wasiomheshimu. Lakini alimlinda Nuhu pamoja na watu wengine saba. Nuhu ndiye aliyewaeleza watu habari za haki. \v 6 Mungu aliihukumu pia miji ya Sodoma na Gomora. Aliiteketeza kwa moto mpaka yakabaki majivu tu. Kwa njia hiyo alionyesha yatakayowapata watu wasiomheshimu. \v 7 Lakini Mungu alimwokoa Lutu, mtu mwenye haki. Lutu alihuzunika sana kwa sababu ya maisha yasiyo na haya ya watu waovu waliomzunguka. \v 8 Siku baada ya siku mtu huyo mwenye haki aliishi kati yao, na maovu aliyoyaona na kuyasikia yalimuumiza moyoni. \v 9 Basi mnaweza kuwa na hakika na jambo hili: Bwana anajua jinsi ya kuwaokoa watu wanaomheshimu wanapopitia nyakati ngumu. Tena anajua jinsi ya kuwaweka waovu chini ya adhabu mpaka siku atakapowahukumu. \v 10 Hili ni kweli hasa kwa wale wanaofuata tamaa mbaya za mwili zinazowafanya wawe najisi, na wanaodharau mamlaka ya Bwana.

decisions.choice: one long "if ... then" sentence: if God did all this (verses 4-8), then the Lord knows how to rescue the godly and to keep the wicked for judgment (verse 9)
decisions.reason: Εἰ ("if") governs four examples: the angels, the flood, Sodom and Gomorrah, and Lot. The main clause comes only in verse 9, οἶδεν κύριος ("the Lord knows"). The examples pair judgment with rescue: Noah is kept safe in the flood, Lot is rescued from Sodom. That is the point of verse 9, and the answer to those who say God's judgment is idle (verse 3).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "chains" of gloom
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads σειραῖς, "with chains". A number of important early manuscripts have a word spelled almost the same that means "pits" or "underground storage pits"; the two differ by a letter or two. "Chains" agrees with Jude 6 ("in eternal bonds under gloom"), which may have influenced copyists, or may be the source of this verse. Either way the angels are held in darkness until judgment. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: Tartarus: the deepest place of the underworld, a prison of punishment
alternatives: hell, in the sense of the final punishment
decisions.reason: ταρταρώσας is a verb, "to put into Tartarus", found only here in the Bible. In Greek stories Tartarus was the deepest part of the underworld, far below Hades, where the gods had imprisoned the rebel Titans. Jewish writing in Greek used the name too: the Greek Old Testament has it in Job 40:20, 41:24 and Proverbs 30:16, and the Greek text of 1 Enoch 20:2 names Tartarus among the places over which an angel is set. Peter uses a word his readers knew for the prison of rebel spirits; it is a holding place before the judgment, not the final judgment itself.

decisions.choice: angels who sinned: the text does not say what their sin was; it is most likely the story of Genesis 6:1-4 as Jewish tradition told it
alternatives: the first rebellion of angels against God, before the creation of humankind
decisions.reason: Jude 6 speaks of angels "who did not keep their own position", kept in bonds under gloom for the judgment. Jewish writings of the period, such as 1 Enoch 6-16, read Genesis 6:1-4 as the sin of angels who took human wives before the flood, and say they were bound in darkness until judgment. 2 Peter moves straight on from the angels to the flood, the same order as Genesis 6. The text itself names only their sin and their punishment.

decisions.choice: the ancient world; a world of the ungodly: humankind before the flood
decisions.reason: ἀρχαίου κόσμου is the world of people that lived before the flood (Genesis 6:5-7). In 3:6 Peter says "the world that then was" was destroyed by water. Here world means the people in it, not the earth itself.

decisions.choice: Noah, the eighth: Noah and seven others; a herald of righteousness: one who announced what is right before God
decisions.reason: "The eighth" is a Greek way of saying "one of eight": Noah, his wife, his three sons and their wives (Genesis 7:13; 1 Peter 3:20). Genesis records no sermon of Noah, but Jewish tradition, for example Josephus (Antiquities 1.74), says he urged the people of his time to change their ways. κήρυκα is a herald, one who publicly proclaims a message.

decisions.choice: Sodom and Gomorrah: burned to ashes (Genesis 19:24-29), made an example of God's judgment
decisions.reason: Genesis 19 tells how God rained fire and sulfur on the cities. Later Scripture makes them the standing example of judgment (Deuteronomy 29:23; Isaiah 1:9; Matthew 10:15; Jude 7). τεφρώσας means to burn to ashes; ὑπόδειγμα is a pattern or warning set up for others to see.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "condemned to overthrow"; "an example of what is coming for the ungodly"
alternatives: "an example to those who would live ungodly lives"
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts lack καταστροφῇ ("to overthrow"); the SBLGNT keeps it. In the same verse manuscripts are divided between ἀσεβέσιν ("for the ungodly") and a verb form meaning "to be ungodly", which gives "an example to those about to live ungodly lives". The sense is close either way: Sodom warns those who live without God. Reviewers must check these against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: righteous Lot
decisions.reason: Genesis does not call Lot righteous, and shows his failings (Genesis 19:8, 30-36). But Abraham pleads for the righteous in Sodom (Genesis 18:23-32), and the angels bring Lot out (Genesis 19:15-16); Wisdom of Solomon 10:6 also calls him "a righteous man" rescued from the fire. Peter stresses that God rescued him and that he was grieved by what he saw.

decisions.choice: verse 8 is an aside, and in it Lot torments his own soul
alternatives: Lot's soul was tormented by the lawless deeds
decisions.reason: γὰρ ("for") opens an explanation of verse 7. The verb ἐβασάνιζεν is active, with ὁ δίκαιος ("the righteous man") as its subject: day after day he tormented his own righteous soul over what he saw and heard. βλέμματι καὶ ἀκοῇ ("by seeing and hearing") most likely says how the deeds reached him.

decisions.choice: trial: a time of testing and pressure, like Lot's in Sodom
decisions.reason: πειρασμός can mean testing or temptation. Set beside Lot's distress, it means the hard times of those who stay faithful among the ungodly (compare 1 Peter 1:6; 4:12).

decisions.choice: keep the unrighteous under punishment until the day of judgment
alternatives: keep the unrighteous to be punished on the day of judgment
decisions.reason: κολαζομένους is a present participle, "being punished", so the natural sense is that the wicked are already under punishment while they are kept for the final day, as the angels of verse 4 are held in chains "being kept for judgment". Others read it as the purpose of the keeping: they are kept for punishment on that day. Both say their judgment is certain.

decisions.choice: those who go after the flesh in defiling desire: an echo of Sodom
decisions.reason: "After the flesh" points back to Sodom: Jude 7 says the people of Sodom "went after other flesh". Flesh here is human nature bent on its own desires, and μιασμοῦ is what makes a person unclean. Peter turns from the examples to the false teachers themselves.

decisions.choice: lordship: the Lord's authority
alternatives: angelic powers (the "glorious ones" of the next sentence)
decisions.reason: κυριότητος comes from the word for lord. Since the false teachers "deny the Master" (verse 1), the most likely sense is that they despise the Lord's rule over them. In Ephesians 1:21 and Colossians 1:16 the same word names a rank of spiritual powers, and the next sentence speaks of heavenly beings, so some read it that way; Jude 8 has the same pair of ideas.

decisions.choice: verses 4-8 as statements, then "If God did all this, then the Lord knows" (B); "So you can be sure of this" (R)
alternatives: keeping "if" at the start and holding the main clause back to verse 9
decisions.reason: The Greek holds its main clause back for six verses. Balanced and Readable state the examples first and then draw the conclusion, which says the same as the conditional (m1). Literal keeps the Greek shape.

decisions.choice: Noah with seven others
decisions.reason: "The eighth" means one of eight (m6); Balanced and Readable say so.

decisions.choice: Tartarus (all levels); "the deepest prison" added in Readable
decisions.reason: "Hell" would suggest the final punishment, which Peter places later, at the judgment (m3). The name is kept, and Readable explains it.

decisions.choice: people who honor him; people who did not honor him
decisions.reason: "Godly" and "ungodly" are church words; Readable says what they mean: living with reverence for God, or without it.

decisions.choice: the Lord's authority
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the sense chosen in m14; Literal keeps "lordship".

decisions.choice: piadosos / impíos
alternatives: los que temen a Dios / los que no temen a Dios
decisions.reason: "Piadoso" is the adjective of "piedad", the settled word for godliness in Peter's letters, and "impío" is its opposite, so Literal and Balanced keep the pair. Readable says what they mean, as the English Readable does: "los que (no) lo honran".

decisions.choice: watauwa / wasiomcha Mungu
decisions.reason: "Watauwa" (the godly) goes with "utauwa", the settled word for godliness in Peter's letters. For the ungodly Swahili has no matching negative, so Literal and Balanced say "wasiomcha Mungu" (those who do not fear God), the usual phrase. Readable says "wanaomheshimu" / "wasiomheshimu" (who honor him / who do not), as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: nafsi
decisions.reason: "Roho" is kept for the Spirit and for spirit; the Greek word here is the self, a person's inner life, which Swahili calls "nafsi".

source.text: Τολμηταὶ, αὐθάδεις, δόξας οὐ τρέμουσιν, βλασφημοῦντες, ὅπου ἄγγελοι ἰσχύϊ καὶ δυνάμει μείζονες ὄντες οὐ φέρουσιν κατ’ αὐτῶν βλάσφημον κρίσιν.

records.literal_gloss: Daring [ones], self-willed, glorious [ones] they do not tremble blaspheming, \v 11 where angels in strength and power greater being not do bring against them a blasphemous judgment.

en.L: Daring, self-willed, they do not tremble [when] blaspheming glorious ones, \v 11 whereas angels, though greater in strength and power, do not bring a blasphemous judgment against them.
en.B: Reckless and arrogant, they are not afraid to slander the glorious ones, \v 11 when even angels, who are greater in strength and power, do not bring a slanderous judgment against them.
en.R: These teachers are bold and stubborn. They are not afraid to insult glorious beings in the heavenly world. \v 11 Yet angels are stronger and more powerful than these teachers, and even they do not insult those beings when they accuse them.

es.L: Atrevidos, arrogantes, no tiemblan [al] blasfemar contra los gloriosos, \v 11 mientras que los ángeles, aunque son mayores en fuerza y poder, no traen contra ellos un juicio blasfemo.
es.B: Temerarios y arrogantes, no tienen miedo de calumniar a los seres gloriosos, \v 11 cuando ni siquiera los ángeles, que son mayores en fuerza y poder, presentan contra ellos un juicio calumnioso.
es.R: Estos maestros son atrevidos y tercos. No tienen miedo de insultar a seres gloriosos del mundo celestial. \v 11 En cambio, los ángeles son más fuertes y poderosos que estos maestros, y ni siquiera ellos insultan a esos seres cuando los acusan.

sw.L: Wenye kuthubutu, wakaidi, hawatetemeki wakiwakufuru wenye utukufu, \v 11 ilhali malaika, ingawa ni wakuu zaidi kwa nguvu na uwezo, hawaleti juu yao hukumu ya kukufuru.
sw.B: Wakiwa jasiri kupita kiasi na wenye kiburi, hawaogopi kuwatukana wenye utukufu, \v 11 wakati hata malaika, walio wakuu zaidi kwa nguvu na uwezo, hawaleti juu yao hukumu ya matusi.
sw.R: Walimu hao ni wajeuri na wakaidi. Hawaogopi kuwatukana viumbe wenye utukufu katika ulimwengu wa mbinguni. \v 11 Lakini malaika wana nguvu na uwezo zaidi kuliko walimu hao, na hata wao hawawatukani viumbe hao wanapowashtaki.

decisions.choice: a new sentence that describes the people of verse 10a
decisions.reason: Τολμηταὶ and αὐθάδεις are nominatives with no verb of their own; they open a new sentence with an exclamation about "those who go after the flesh". αὐθάδης is one who pleases himself and will not be told.

decisions.choice: glorious ones: heavenly beings, most likely evil angelic powers
decisions.reason: δόξας ("glories") is used for angelic beings in Jewish writing, and Jude 8 uses it the same way. Since angels themselves refuse to accuse them abusively (verse 11), and Jude 9 gives the example of the archangel Michael and the devil, they are probably fallen powers. The false teachers mock spiritual powers they do not understand (verse 12).

decisions.choice: against them: against the glorious ones
decisions.reason: κατ αὐτῶν most naturally points back to the glorious ones: even angels do not bring an insulting charge against them. Jude 9 says the same of Michael, who "did not dare" bring a slanderous judgment against the devil, but said "The Lord rebuke you" (compare Zechariah 3:2). Some read "them" as the false teachers, whom the angels do not accuse before the Lord.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: no "before the Lord"
alternatives: "a slanderous judgment against them before the Lord"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "before the Lord" (or "from the Lord") after "judgment". Some early witnesses lack it, and the SBLGNT leaves it out. The words make the angels' restraint a matter of respect for God's court. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: a parallel to Jude 8-9
decisions.reason: Jude 8-9 has the same contrast, and names the angel: Michael, disputing with the devil over the body of Moses. 2 Peter makes the point without the story.

decisions.choice: blaspheming; blasphemous (L); slander; slanderous (B); insult (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 2, Literal keeps the Greek word, and Balanced and Readable use words that current English uses for speech against beings other than God.

decisions.choice: These teachers; stronger and more powerful than these teachers
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject and says whom the angels are greater than; the comparison is implied in the Greek.

decisions.choice: glorious beings in the heavenly world
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of beings are meant (m2) and keeps the word "glorious".

source.text: οὗτοι δέ, ὡς ἄλογα ζῷα γεγεννημένα φυσικὰ εἰς ἅλωσιν καὶ φθοράν, ἐν οἷς ἀγνοοῦσιν βλασφημοῦντες, ἐν τῇ φθορᾷ αὐτῶν καὶ φθαρήσονται, ἀδικούμενοι μισθὸν ἀδικίας·

records.literal_gloss: These but, as irrational animals having been born creatures of instinct for capture and destruction, in what they are ignorant of blaspheming, in the destruction of them also will be destroyed, \v 13 being wronged [as the] wage of wrongdoing;

en.L: But these [people], like irrational animals, born as creatures of nature for capture and destruction, blaspheming in matters they do not understand, will also be destroyed in their destruction, \v 13 being wronged [as] the wage of wrongdoing.
en.B: But these people are like animals that cannot reason, ruled by instinct, born to be caught and killed. They slander what they do not understand, and like those animals they too will be destroyed, \v 13 suffering harm as payment for the harm they have done.
en.R: But these people are like wild animals that cannot think. Such animals act only by instinct, and they are born to be caught and killed. These people insult things they do not understand. And like those animals, they will be destroyed. \v 13 They will be paid back with harm for the harm they have done.

es.L: Pero estos, como animales irracionales, nacidos como criaturas del instinto para ser atrapados y destruidos, blasfemando en lo que ignoran, también serán destruidos en su destrucción, \v 13 padeciendo injusticia [como] salario de [su] injusticia.
es.B: Pero estas personas son como animales que no razonan, guiados por el instinto, nacidos para ser atrapados y muertos. Calumnian lo que no entienden, y como esos animales, también ellos serán destruidos, \v 13 sufriendo daño como pago por el daño que han hecho.
es.R: Pero estas personas son como animales salvajes que no pueden pensar. Esos animales actúan solo por instinto, y nacen para que los atrapen y los maten. Estas personas insultan cosas que no entienden. Y como esos animales, serán destruidas. \v 13 Recibirán daño como pago por el daño que han hecho.

sw.L: Lakini hawa, kama wanyama wasio na busara, waliozaliwa kama viumbe vya silika kwa ajili ya kukamatwa na kuangamizwa, wakikufuru katika mambo wasiyoyajua, wataangamizwa pia katika maangamizi yao, \v 13 wakitendewa udhalimu [kama] malipo ya udhalimu.
sw.B: Lakini watu hawa ni kama wanyama wasioweza kufikiri, wanaotawaliwa na silika, waliozaliwa ili wakamatwe na kuuawa. Wanatukana wasiyoyaelewa, na kama wanyama hao, wao pia wataangamizwa, \v 13 wakipata madhara kama malipo ya madhara waliyoyatenda.
sw.R: Lakini watu hawa ni kama wanyama wa porini wasioweza kufikiri. Wanyama hao hufanya mambo kwa silika tu, nao huzaliwa ili wakamatwe na kuuawa. Watu hawa wanatukana mambo wasiyoyaelewa. Na kama wanyama hao, wataangamizwa. \v 13 Watalipwa madhara kwa madhara waliyoyatenda.

decisions.choice: they will be destroyed in their destruction: they will perish as the animals perish
alternatives: they will perish in their own corruption
decisions.reason: αὐτῶν most naturally refers to the animals just named: the false teachers will be destroyed just as such animals are. φθορά can also mean corruption, as in 1:4 and 2:19, so the phrase may also hint that their own rot destroys them. The wordplay in Greek (destruction, will be destroyed) is deliberate.

decisions.choice: suffering wrong as the wage of wrongdoing: paid back in kind for the wrong they have done
decisions.reason: ἀδικούμενοι ("being wronged") and ἀδικίας ("wrongdoing") come from the same root: the wages they earn by wrong are wrong done to them. The same "wage of wrongdoing" is what Balaam loved (verse 15).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "suffering wrong"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read a different verb here, "receiving" (the wage of wrongdoing). The SBLGNT reads ἀδικούμενοι, "suffering wrong", the harder reading with its wordplay, which copyists may have smoothed. The meaning is close either way: they get what they have earned. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: a parallel to Jude 10
decisions.reason: Jude 10 also says that such people slander what they do not understand, and are destroyed by what they know by instinct, like irrational animals.

decisions.choice: like those animals
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the comparison chosen in m1.

decisions.choice: padeciendo injusticia [como] salario de [su] injusticia (L); daño ... por el daño (B, R)
decisions.reason: Each level keeps the play on one root (m2). Literal uses "injusticia", the settled word beside "justicia", which also lets verse 15 say Balaam loved "el salario de la injusticia"; Balanced and Readable use the plainer pair "daño" / "el daño que han hecho".

decisions.choice: wakitendewa udhalimu [kama] malipo ya udhalimu (L); madhara ... madhara (B, R)
decisions.reason: Swahili keeps the play on one root (m2): Literal with "udhalimu", the settled word beside "haki", which verse 15 repeats for Balaam ("malipo ya udhalimu"); Balanced and Readable with the plainer "madhara" (harm).

source.text: ἡδονὴν ἡγούμενοι τὴν ἐν ἡμέρᾳ τρυφήν, σπίλοι καὶ μῶμοι ἐντρυφῶντες ἐν ταῖς ἀπάταις αὐτῶν συνευωχούμενοι ὑμῖν, ὀφθαλμοὺς ἔχοντες μεστοὺς μοιχαλίδος καὶ ἀκαταπαύστους ἁμαρτίας, δελεάζοντες ψυχὰς ἀστηρίκτους, καρδίαν γεγυμνασμένην πλεονεξίας ἔχοντες, κατάρας τέκνα, καταλιπόντες εὐθεῖαν ὁδὸν ἐπλανήθησαν, ἐξακολουθήσαντες τῇ ὁδῷ τοῦ Βαλαὰμ τοῦ Βοσὸρ ὃς μισθὸν ἀδικίας ἠγάπησεν ἔλεγξιν δὲ ἔσχεν ἰδίας παρανομίας·

records.literal_gloss: pleasure considering the in daytime reveling, stains and blemishes, reveling in the deceptions of them feasting together with you, \v 14 eyes having full of an adulteress and unceasing from sin, enticing souls unsteady, a heart trained in greed having, of a curse children; \v 15 having left [the] straight way they went astray, having followed the way of the Balaam the [son] of Bosor, who [the] wage of wrongdoing loved, \v 16 but a rebuke he had of [his] own transgression;

en.L: Considering luxury by day [a] pleasure, [they are] stains and blemishes, indulging in their deceptions as they feast together with you, \v 14 having eyes full of an adulteress and never ceasing from sin, luring unstable souls, having a heart exercised in greed, children of a curse; \v 15 leaving the straight way, they went astray, following the way of Balaam, the [son] of Bosor, who loved the wage of wrongdoing, \v 16 but he received a rebuke for his own transgression.
en.B: They think it a pleasure to indulge themselves in broad daylight. They are stains and blemishes, enjoying their deceptions while they eat with you at your meals. \v 14 Their eyes are always on the lookout for adultery and never have enough of sin. They lure people who are not yet steady. They have practiced greed until their hearts are skilled in it. They are people under a curse! \v 15 They have abandoned the straight road and lost their way, following the road of Balaam son of Bosor, who loved the pay he could get for doing wrong. \v 16 But he was confronted with his own lawbreaking.
en.R: They think it is fun to party wildly even in the daytime. They are like dirty stains at your meals, enjoying their tricks while they eat with you. \v 14 They are always looking for someone to commit adultery with, and they never stop sinning. They trap people who are not yet standing firm. They have trained their hearts to always want more. God's curse is on them! \v 15 They have left the right road and gone the wrong way. They have followed the road of Balaam son of Bosor. He loved the money he could get by doing wrong. \v 16 But he was scolded for the wrong he did.

es.L: Considerando placer el lujo de día, [son] manchas y defectos, deleitándose en sus engaños mientras banquetean con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, \v 14 teniendo ojos llenos de adúltera y que no cesan de pecar, seduciendo a almas inestables, teniendo un corazón ejercitado en la avaricia, hijos de maldición; \v 15 dejando el camino recto, se extraviaron, siguiendo el camino de Balaam, [hijo] de Bosor, que amó el salario de la injusticia, \v 16 pero recibió reprensión por su propia transgresión.
es.B: Consideran un placer entregarse a los lujos a plena luz del día. Son manchas y defectos, que disfrutan de sus engaños mientras se sientan a comer con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. \v 14 Sus ojos siempre andan buscando adulterio y nunca se sacian de pecar. Seducen a los que todavía no están firmes. Han practicado la avaricia hasta que su corazón se ha vuelto experto en ella. ¡Son gente bajo maldición! \v 15 Han abandonado el camino recto y se han perdido, siguiendo el camino de Balaam hijo de Bosor, que amó la paga que podía obtener haciendo el mal. \v 16 Pero se le echó en cara su propia transgresión de la ley.
es.R: Les parece divertido hacer fiestas desenfrenadas incluso de día. Son como manchas sucias en las comidas {{plural_you:de ustedes|vuestras}}, y disfrutan de sus trampas mientras comen con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. \v 14 Siempre andan buscando con quién cometer adulterio, y nunca dejan de pecar. Atrapan a los que todavía no están firmes. Han entrenado su corazón para querer siempre más. ¡La maldición de Dios está sobre ellos! \v 15 Han dejado el buen camino y se han ido por el camino equivocado. Han seguido el camino de Balaam hijo de Bosor. Él amó el dinero que podía ganar haciendo el mal. \v 16 Pero fue reprendido por el mal que hizo.

sw.L: Wakiona anasa ya mchana kuwa raha, [wao ni] madoa na kasoro, wakijifurahisha katika udanganyifu wao wanapokula karamu pamoja nanyi, \v 14 wakiwa na macho yaliyojaa mzinzi na yasiyoacha dhambi, wakizivuta kwa chambo nafsi zisizo thabiti, wakiwa na moyo uliozoezwa uchoyo, watoto wa laana; \v 15 wakiiacha njia iliyonyooka walipotea, wakiifuata njia ya Balaamu [mwana] wa Bosori, aliyependa malipo ya udhalimu, \v 16 lakini alikemewa kwa ukiukaji wake mwenyewe wa sheria.
sw.B: Wanaona ni raha kujifurahisha waziwazi mchana. Wao ni madoa na kasoro, wakifurahia udanganyifu wao wanapokula pamoja nanyi. \v 14 Macho yao daima yanatafuta uzinzi, wala hayatosheki na dhambi. Wanawavuta kwa chambo watu ambao bado hawajasimama imara. Wamezoea uchoyo mpaka mioyo yao imebobea ndani yake. Ni watu walio chini ya laana! \v 15 Wameiacha njia iliyonyooka, wakapotea, wakaifuata njia ya Balaamu mwana wa Bosori, aliyependa malipo aliyoweza kupata kwa kutenda mabaya. \v 16 Lakini alikemewa kwa kosa lake la kuvunja sheria.
sw.R: Wanaona ni jambo la kufurahisha kufanya sherehe bila kiasi hata mchana. Wao ni kama madoa machafu katika milo yenu, wakifurahia hila zao wanapokula pamoja nanyi. \v 14 Daima wanatafuta mtu wa kuzini naye, wala hawaachi kutenda dhambi. Wanawanasa watu ambao bado hawajasimama imara. Wamezoeza mioyo yao kutamani zaidi siku zote. Laana ya Mungu iko juu yao! \v 15 Wameiacha njia sahihi na kwenda njia mbaya. Wameifuata njia ya Balaamu mwana wa Bosori. Yeye alipenda fedha ambazo angeweza kupata kwa kutenda mabaya. \v 16 Lakini alikaripiwa kwa ubaya aliofanya.

decisions.choice: a new record begins after the raised dot in verse 13, and the record ends at the raised dot in verse 16
alternatives: verses 12-16 as one record, as the skeleton had it
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT puts a raised dot after ἀδικίας and another after παρανομίας. The clauses from ἡδονὴν to the end of verse 14 are participles whose main verb is ἐπλανήθησαν ("they went astray") in verse 15, so they stand on their own as one sentence. The words about Balaam's donkey in verse 16 have their own subject and verb and form the next record.

decisions.choice: revel in the daytime: indulge openly, in broad daylight
alternatives: revel for a day: short-lived pleasure
decisions.reason: ἐν ἡμέρᾳ most likely means "by day": even the pagan world thought daytime drinking and feasting shameful (compare Isaiah 5:11; Acts 2:15; Romans 13:13). It could also mean pleasure that lasts only a day, set against the coming judgment.

decisions.choice: stains and blemishes: they spoil the church's fellowship
decisions.reason: σπίλος is a stain and μῶμος a blemish or defect. Peter calls believers to be found "without stain and without blemish" (3:14), the words used for Christ the lamb (1 Peter 1:19); the false teachers are the reverse. Jude 12 uses a word that sounds alike but means hidden reefs.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "in their deceptions"
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads ἀπάταις, "deceptions". Several manuscripts read a word that differs by a few letters, "love feasts", which is what Jude 12 has. The SBLGNT reading may play on that word: their "love feasts" have become "deceptions". Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: feasting with you: sharing the church's common meals
decisions.reason: The early churches ate together, and the meal could include the Lord's Supper (Acts 2:46; 1 Corinthians 11:20-22). Jude 12 calls these meals love feasts. The false teachers were not outsiders; they sat at the same table.

decisions.choice: eyes full of an adulteress: they look at every woman as a partner for adultery
decisions.reason: μοιχαλίδος is "an adulteress". The picture is of eyes that cannot look at a woman without desire (compare Matthew 5:28). ἀκαταπαύστους ἁμαρτίας adds that such eyes never rest from sinning.

decisions.choice: enticing unsteady souls: luring people who are not yet firm in the faith
decisions.reason: δελεάζω comes from the word for bait, as in fishing or trapping; it comes again in verse 18. ἀστήρικτος means not made firm. Peter tells his readers to guard against losing their own firm footing (3:17).

decisions.choice: children of a curse: people under God's curse
decisions.reason: "Children of" is a Hebrew way of saying that someone belongs to or is marked by something (compare "children of wrath", Ephesians 2:3). The curse is God's judgment on them.

decisions.choice: the way of Balaam: the prophet who was willing to curse Israel for pay (Numbers 22-24)
decisions.reason: Balak king of Moab hired Balaam to curse Israel, and he set out for the fee (Numbers 22:7, 17; Deuteronomy 23:4). Later Scripture also blames his advice for leading Israel into immorality and idolatry (Numbers 31:16; Revelation 2:14). Jude 11 likewise names "Balaam's error for pay". The false teachers, greedy and luring others into sin, follow his road.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "Bosor"
decisions.reason: In Numbers Balaam is the son of Beor. The SBLGNT reads Βοσὸρ, "Bosor", which is attested only here; at least one important early manuscript reads "Beor", which looks like a correction to agree with Numbers. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the wage of wrongdoing: the pay he could get for doing wrong
decisions.reason: The same words as in verse 13. Balaam loved the reward for wrong; the false teachers will receive the reward of wrong.

decisions.choice: several short sentences
decisions.reason: The Greek strings a dozen descriptions on to one main verb in verse 15. Balanced and Readable give each its own sentence; Literal keeps the chain.

decisions.choice: always on the lookout for adultery (B); always looking for someone to commit adultery with (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the picture means (m6).

decisions.choice: God's curse is on them
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom and names whose curse it is (m8).

decisions.choice: las comidas {{plural_you:de ustedes|vuestras}}
decisions.reason: With ustedes, "sus comidas" could be read as the false teachers' meals. "De ustedes" makes clear that the meals are the readers' own church meals (m5).

decisions.choice: Bosori
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads "Bosor" (m10), so Swahili gives that name a Swahili ending, "Bosori". "Beori", the familiar Swahili form from Numbers, would silently follow the other reading. A reviewer should confirm the form.

source.text: ὑποζύγιον ἄφωνον ἐν ἀνθρώπου φωνῇ φθεγξάμενον ἐκώλυσεν τὴν τοῦ προφήτου παραφρονίαν.

records.literal_gloss: a beast of burden voiceless in a man's voice having spoken restrained the of the prophet madness.

en.L: A voiceless beast of burden, speaking with a human voice, restrained the prophet's madness.
en.B: A donkey, which has no power of speech, talked in a human voice and stopped the prophet in his madness.
en.R: His donkey, which could not talk, spoke to him with a human voice. It stopped the prophet from doing his crazy plan.

es.L: Una bestia de carga muda, hablando con voz humana, refrenó la locura del profeta.
es.B: Una burra, que no puede hablar, habló con voz humana y frenó al profeta en su locura.
es.R: Su burra, que no podía hablar, le habló con voz humana. Así impidió que el profeta llevara a cabo su loco plan.

sw.L: Mnyama wa kubeba mizigo asiye na sauti, akisema kwa sauti ya mwanadamu, alikomesha wazimu wa nabii.
sw.B: Punda, ambaye hawezi kuongea, alizungumza kwa sauti ya binadamu, akamzuia nabii katika wazimu wake.
sw.R: Punda wake, ambaye hakuweza kuongea, alizungumza naye kwa sauti ya binadamu. Akamzuia nabii huyo asitekeleze mpango wake wa kichaa.

decisions.choice: this clause is its own record
alternatives: part of the sentence of verses 13-16
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT puts a raised dot before ὑποζύγιον, and the clause has its own subject and verb (ἐκώλυσεν, "restrained"); see the previous record.

decisions.choice: Balaam's donkey (Numbers 22:21-35)
decisions.reason: On the road the donkey saw the angel of the Lord that Balaam could not see, and God opened its mouth to speak to him (Numbers 22:28-30). The irony is sharp: an animal that cannot speak sees more than the prophet, and checks him.

decisions.choice: beast of burden: a donkey
decisions.reason: ὑποζύγιον means an animal under the yoke, a pack or riding animal. In Numbers it is Balaam's own female donkey.

decisions.choice: madness: being out of one's right mind
decisions.reason: παραφρονία means losing one's senses. Balaam's plan to curse the people God had blessed, for money, was folly of that kind.

decisions.choice: donkey
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the animal, as Numbers 22 does; Literal keeps the general word.

source.text: Οὗτοί εἰσιν πηγαὶ ἄνυδροι καὶ ὁμίχλαι ὑπὸ λαίλαπος ἐλαυνόμεναι, οἷς ὁ ζόφος τοῦ σκότους τετήρηται.

records.literal_gloss: These are springs waterless and mists by a squall being driven, for whom the gloom of the darkness has been kept.

en.L: These are springs without water and mists driven by a squall, for whom the gloom of darkness has been kept.
en.B: These people are springs that have run dry, mists chased along by a squall. The blackest darkness is being kept for them.
en.R: These teachers are like springs with no water in them. They are like mist that a storm blows away. A place of deep darkness is being kept ready for them.

es.L: Estos son fuentes sin agua y nieblas arrastradas por una borrasca, para quienes ha sido reservada la oscuridad de las tinieblas.
es.B: Estas personas son manantiales secos, neblinas empujadas por una tormenta. Para ellos está reservada la más negra oscuridad.
es.R: Estos maestros son como manantiales sin agua. Son como neblina que se lleva una tormenta. Hay un lugar de oscuridad profunda que ya está preparado para ellos.

sw.L: Hawa ni chemchemi zisizo na maji na ukungu unaosukumwa na dhoruba, ambao kwa ajili yao utusitusi wa giza umehifadhiwa.
sw.B: Watu hawa ni chemchemi zilizokauka, ukungu unaofukuzwa na upepo mkali. Giza jeusi kabisa limewekwa kwa ajili yao.
sw.R: Walimu hao ni kama chemchemi zisizo na maji ndani yake. Ni kama ukungu unaopeperushwa na dhoruba. Mahali pa giza nene pameandaliwa tayari kwa ajili yao.

decisions.choice: springs without water, mists driven by a storm: they promise refreshment and give none
decisions.reason: A spring that has dried up disappoints a thirsty traveler; mist driven off by a squall brings no rain. Jude 12-13 uses similar pictures: clouds without water carried along by winds.

decisions.choice: the gloom of darkness: the place of punishment, already reserved for them
decisions.reason: ζόφος is the darkness of the underworld, as in verse 4. τετήρηται is perfect: the place is already set aside and waiting, as verse 3 says their destruction is not asleep.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: no "forever"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "forever" at the end, the wording of Jude 13. Earlier manuscripts lack it, and the SBLGNT leaves it out. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: These people (B); These teachers are like (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who is meant, and Readable makes the pictures comparisons.

source.text: ὑπέρογκα γὰρ ματαιότητος φθεγγόμενοι δελεάζουσιν ἐν ἐπιθυμίαις σαρκὸς ἀσελγείαις τοὺς ὀλίγως ἀποφεύγοντας τοὺς ἐν πλάνῃ ἀναστρεφομένους, ἐλευθερίαν αὐτοῖς ἐπαγγελλόμενοι, αὐτοὶ δοῦλοι ὑπάρχοντες τῆς φθορᾶς·

records.literal_gloss: Swollen [words] for of emptiness uttering they entice with desires of flesh, with sensualities, those barely escaping from those in error living, \v 19 freedom to them promising, themselves slaves being of the corruption;

en.L: For, uttering swollen [words] of emptiness, they entice with desires of the flesh, with sensualities, those who are barely escaping from those who live in error, \v 19 promising them freedom, while they themselves are slaves of corruption.
en.B: They speak big, empty words, and with the flesh and its shameless desires as bait they lure people who are only just getting away from those who are living astray. \v 19 They promise them freedom, but they themselves are slaves of corruption.
en.R: They boast with big words that mean nothing. They use sinful desires and shameless living as bait to trap people who have only just started to get away from those who live wrong lives. \v 19 They promise these people freedom. But they themselves are slaves of corruption, the evil that is ruining them.

es.L: Porque, profiriendo [palabras] infladas de vanidad, seducen con deseos de la carne, con desenfrenos, a los que apenas escapan de los que viven en el error, \v 19 prometiéndoles libertad, mientras ellos mismos son esclavos de la corrupción.
es.B: Hablan palabras grandes y vacías, y usando como cebo la carne y sus deseos desvergonzados atraen a los que apenas se están alejando de quienes viven extraviados. \v 19 Les prometen libertad, pero ellos mismos son esclavos de la corrupción.
es.R: Se jactan con palabras grandes que no significan nada. Usan los malos deseos y la vida desvergonzada como cebo para atrapar a los que apenas han empezado a alejarse de la gente que vive mal. \v 19 A estas personas les prometen libertad. Pero ellos mismos son esclavos de la corrupción, la maldad que los está arruinando.

sw.L: Kwa maana, wakitamka [maneno] yaliyovimba ya ubatili, wanawavuta kwa chambo kwa tamaa za mwili, kwa matendo ya ukosefu wa haya, wale wanaoponyoka kwa shida kutoka kwa wale wanaoishi katika upotevu, \v 19 wakiwaahidi uhuru, ilhali wao wenyewe ni watumwa wa uharibifu.
sw.B: Wanasema maneno makubwa yasiyo na maana, na kwa chambo cha tamaa za mwili zisizo na haya wanawanasa watu ambao ndio kwanza wanaanza kuwakimbia wale wanaoishi katika upotevu. \v 19 Wanawaahidi uhuru, lakini wao wenyewe ni watumwa wa uharibifu.
sw.R: Wanajisifu kwa maneno makubwa yasiyo na maana yoyote. Wanatumia tamaa mbaya na maisha yasiyo na haya kama chambo ili kuwanasa watu ambao ndio kwanza wameanza kuwakimbia wale wanaoishi maisha mabaya. \v 19 Wanawaahidi watu hao uhuru. Lakini wao wenyewe ni watumwa wa uharibifu, yaani uovu unaowaangamiza.

decisions.choice: swollen words of emptiness: boastful talk with nothing in it
decisions.reason: ὑπέρογκος means swollen, inflated, and so arrogant or high-sounding; ματαιότης is emptiness, futility. Jude 16 also says such people speak arrogant words.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "barely", "only just" escaping
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads ὀλίγως, "barely" or "only just". Many manuscripts read a different adverb meaning "really" or "truly". With "barely", the targets are new believers who have only just left their old life, and so are easy prey ("unstable souls", verse 14). Some manuscripts also read "have escaped" for "are escaping". Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: those who live in error: the world the new believers have just left
decisions.reason: τοὺς ἐν πλάνῃ ἀναστρεφομένους are the people still living astray from God; the new believers are getting away from them and from their way of life.

decisions.choice: slaves of corruption: owned and controlled by the decay that is destroying them
decisions.reason: A δοῦλος belonged to a master and could not leave. The irony is that the teachers who promise freedom are themselves owned by corruption (φθορᾶς), the moral rot that leads to ruin (1:4; 2:12). Jesus says that whoever practices sin is a slave of sin (John 8:34; compare Romans 6:16).

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it for slavery to corruption set against freedom: the verse turns on that contrast and on being owned (m4).

decisions.choice: corruption, the evil that is ruining them
decisions.reason: Readable keeps "corruption" and explains it.

source.text: ᾧ γάρ τις ἥττηται, τούτῳ καὶ δεδούλωται.

records.literal_gloss: By what for someone has been overcome, to this also he has been enslaved.

en.L: For by what anyone has been overcome, to this {{gender:they have|he has}} also been enslaved.
en.B: For anyone who is overcome by something has become its slave.
en.R: Whatever gets control of people makes them its slaves.

es.L: Porque por lo que alguien ha sido vencido, de eso también ha sido hecho esclavo.
es.B: Porque cualquiera que es vencido por algo queda hecho esclavo de ello.
es.R: Lo que domina a una persona la hace su esclava.

sw.L: Kwa maana kitu ambacho mtu ameshindwa nacho, amekuwa pia mtumwa wa kitu hicho.
sw.B: Kwa maana mtu yeyote anayeshindwa na kitu fulani amekuwa mtumwa wa kitu hicho.
sw.R: Kitu chochote kinachomtawala mtu humfanya mtu huyo kuwa mtumwa wake.

decisions.choice: a new record begins after the raised dot in verse 19
alternatives: verses 18-19 as one record, as the skeleton had it
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT puts a raised dot after φθορᾶς. The clause that follows is a complete saying with its own verbs, joined by γάρ ("for"), and stands on its own.

decisions.choice: a saying from war: the defeated become the slaves of the one who defeats them
decisions.reason: In the ancient world prisoners of war were commonly sold as slaves. ἥττηται means to be defeated, and δεδούλωται to be made a slave. Whatever a person gives in to becomes that person's master.

decisions.choice: whatever: a thing, though it could also be a person
decisions.reason: ᾧ can be neuter ("by what") or masculine ("by whom"). After "slaves of corruption", a thing is the more natural reading; the saying holds either way.

decisions.choice: {{gender:they have|he has}}
decisions.reason: τις ("anyone") means any person, man or woman; the traditional "he" is the alternative.

decisions.choice: alguien ... ha sido hecho esclavo, no gender setting
decisions.reason: Spanish "alguien" means any person, and the verb needs no subject pronoun, so the sentence has no "he" for the gender setting to change, unlike the English Literal.

decisions.choice: mtu, no gender setting
decisions.reason: Swahili "mtu" means any person, and the verb marks no gender, so Swahili needs no gender span here, unlike the English Literal.

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it for slavery to corruption set against freedom (verse 19a): the defeated become the property of the victor (m2).

source.text: εἰ γὰρ ἀποφυγόντες τὰ μιάσματα τοῦ κόσμου ἐν ἐπιγνώσει τοῦ κυρίου καὶ σωτῆρος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τούτοις δὲ πάλιν ἐμπλακέντες ἡττῶνται, γέγονεν αὐτοῖς τὰ ἔσχατα χείρονα τῶν πρώτων.

records.literal_gloss: If for having escaped the defilements of the world in knowledge of the Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, by these but again having been entangled they are overcome, has become to them the last [things] worse than the first.

en.L: For if, having escaped the defilements of the world through knowledge of the Lord and Savior Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, and again being entangled in these, they are overcome, the last things have become worse for them than the first.
en.B: For if they have escaped the filth of the world by knowing the Lord and Savior Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, and then get tangled up in it again and overcome, they end up worse off than they were at the start.
en.R: These people had escaped the evil things of the world that make people unclean. They did this by coming to know Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, the Lord and Savior. But if they get tangled up in those things again and are beaten by them, they end up worse off than before.

es.L: Porque si, habiendo escapado de las contaminaciones del mundo mediante el conocimiento del Señor y Salvador {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, y enredados otra vez en ellas, son vencidos, las últimas cosas han llegado a ser para ellos peores que las primeras.
es.B: Porque si han escapado de la inmundicia del mundo por conocer al Señor y Salvador {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, y luego se enredan otra vez en ella y son vencidos, terminan peor que al principio.
es.R: Estas personas habían escapado de las cosas malas del mundo que hacen impura a la gente. Lo lograron al llegar a conocer a {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, el Señor y Salvador. Pero si se enredan otra vez en esas cosas y son derrotadas por ellas, terminan peor que antes.

sw.L: Kwa maana ikiwa, baada ya kuziponyoka najisi za ulimwengu kwa ujuzi wa Bwana na Mwokozi Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, wamenaswa tena katika hizo na kushindwa nazo, mambo ya mwisho yamekuwa mabaya zaidi kwao kuliko ya kwanza.
sw.B: Kwa maana ikiwa wameponyoka uchafu wa ulimwengu kwa kumfahamu Bwana na Mwokozi Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, kisha wakanaswa tena humo na kushindwa, wanaishia katika hali mbaya kuliko walivyokuwa mwanzoni.
sw.R: Watu hawa walikuwa wameyaepuka mambo maovu ya ulimwengu yanayowafanya watu kuwa najisi. Waliyaepuka kwa kumfahamu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, Bwana na Mwokozi. Lakini wakinaswa tena na mambo hayo na kushindwa nayo, wanaishia katika hali mbaya kuliko walivyokuwa kabla.

decisions.choice: they: most likely the false teachers, who once knew Christ and have turned back
alternatives: the new believers they lure away (verse 18)
decisions.reason: The subject is not named. The false teachers have been the subject since verse 17, and verse 1 says they deny the Master who bought them, so they once knew him. But the people they lure have also just escaped from those in error (verse 18), and the warning fits them too. The warning is the same whichever group is meant.

decisions.choice: the defilements of the world: the moral filth of a world that lives without God
decisions.reason: μίασμα is what pollutes or stains, related to the word in verse 10. κόσμου here is human society in its rebellion against God, as in 1:4, "the corruption that is in the world".

decisions.choice: knowledge: knowing Christ personally, by which a person is set free
decisions.reason: ἐπίγνωσις is the word Peter uses throughout the letter for the knowledge of God and of Jesus that gives life and godliness (1:2, 3, 8).

decisions.choice: the last things worse than the first: an echo of Jesus' saying about the unclean spirit that returns
decisions.reason: Jesus says of a man whose unclean spirit returns with seven others that his last condition becomes worse than the first (Matthew 12:45; Luke 11:26). The Greek words for last, worse and first are the same.

decisions.choice: Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: overcome
decisions.reason: The same verb as in verse 19 ("has been overcome"), so Literal and Balanced use the same English word to keep the link; Readable says "beaten".

decisions.choice: {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}
decisions.reason: As in Romans, the default is the usual Spanish form of the name, "Jesucristo"; the alternative separates name and title.

source.text: κρεῖττον γὰρ ἦν αὐτοῖς μὴ ἐπεγνωκέναι τὴν ὁδὸν τῆς δικαιοσύνης ἢ ἐπιγνοῦσιν ὑποστρέψαι ἐκ τῆς παραδοθείσης αὐτοῖς ἁγίας ἐντολῆς·

records.literal_gloss: Better for it was for them not to have known the way of the righteousness than having known to turn back from the having been handed down to them holy commandment;

en.L: For better was it for them not to have known the way of righteousness than, having known [it], to turn away from the holy commandment handed down to them.
en.B: They would have been better off never knowing the way of righteousness than knowing it and then abandoning the holy commandment entrusted to them.
en.R: They would have been better off if they had never known the way of righteousness. It is worse to know it and then turn away from the holy command they were given.

es.L: Porque mejor era para ellos no haber conocido el camino de la justicia que, tras conocer[lo], apartarse del santo mandamiento que se les había transmitido.
es.B: Más les habría valido no conocer nunca el camino de la justicia que conocerlo y luego abandonar el santo mandamiento que se les confió.
es.R: Habría sido mejor para ellos no haber conocido nunca el camino de la justicia. Es peor conocerlo y después alejarse del santo mandamiento que recibieron.

sw.L: Kwa maana ilikuwa bora kwao wasiijue njia ya haki, kuliko, wakiisha kuijua, kugeuka mbali na amri takatifu waliyokabidhiwa.
sw.B: Ingekuwa bora kwao kama hawangeijua kamwe njia ya haki, kuliko kuijua kisha kuitupa amri takatifu waliyokabidhiwa.
sw.R: Ingekuwa bora kwao kama hawangeijua kamwe njia ya haki. Ni vibaya zaidi kuijua kisha kuiacha amri takatifu waliyopewa.

decisions.choice: it would have been better: what should have been, but was not
decisions.reason: κρεῖττον ἦν without any further particle is a common way in Greek to say what would have been better, against what in fact happened. It is not a wish that they had never heard, but a measure of how serious turning back is (compare Matthew 26:24).

decisions.choice: the way of righteousness: the way of life that is right before God
decisions.reason: The same "way" as "the way of truth" (verse 2) and "the straight way" (verse 15): the Christian faith as a road one walks. Jesus says that John came "in the way of righteousness" (Matthew 21:32).

decisions.choice: the holy commandment handed down to them: the apostles' teaching about how to live
decisions.reason: παραδοθείσης is the word for passing on tradition (1 Corinthians 15:3; Jude 3). In 3:2 Peter speaks of "the commandment of the Lord and Savior through your apostles": the whole teaching of Christ about a holy life, passed on by the apostles.

decisions.choice: two sentences
decisions.reason: Readable splits the comparison into two short sentences; the meaning is the same.

source.text: συμβέβηκεν αὐτοῖς τὸ τῆς ἀληθοῦς παροιμίας· Κύων ἐπιστρέψας ἐπὶ τὸ ἴδιον ἐξέραμα, καί· Ὗς λουσαμένη εἰς κυλισμὸν βορβόρου.

records.literal_gloss: Has happened to them the [thing] of the true proverb: A dog having turned back to [its] own vomit, and: A sow having washed to rolling of mud.

en.L: To them has happened what the true proverb [says]: A dog, having turned back to its own vomit; and: A sow, having washed, to wallowing in mud.
en.B: The true proverb has come true for them: "A dog goes back to what it threw up," and, "A pig, once washed, goes back to rolling in the mud."
en.R: What the old saying tells is true, and it has happened to them: "A dog goes back to what it threw up." And another saying: "A pig that has been washed goes right back to rolling in the mud."

es.L: Les ha sucedido lo del proverbio verdadero: Un perro, vuelto a su propio vómito; y: Una cerda, lavada, a revolcarse en el lodo.
es.B: Se ha cumplido en ellos el proverbio verdadero: «El perro vuelve a lo que vomitó», y: «El cerdo, una vez lavado, vuelve a revolcarse en el barro».
es.R: Lo que dice el viejo refrán es verdad, y les ha pasado a ellos: «El perro vuelve a lo que vomitó». Y dice otro refrán: «El cerdo que fue lavado vuelve enseguida a revolcarse en el barro».

sw.L: Yamewatokea yale ya methali ya kweli: Mbwa, akiisha kurudi kwenye matapishi yake mwenyewe; na: Nguruwe, akiisha kuoga, kwenye kujigaragaza matopeni.
sw.B: Methali ya kweli imetimia kwao: "Mbwa hurudi kwenye matapishi yake," na, "Nguruwe, akiisha kuoshwa, hurudi kujigaragaza matopeni."
sw.R: Methali ya zamani inasema kweli, na imetimia kwao: "Mbwa hurudi kwenye matapishi yake." Na methali nyingine inasema: "Nguruwe aliyeoshwa hurudi moja kwa moja kujigaragaza matopeni."

decisions.choice: the dog: Proverbs 26:11
decisions.reason: Proverbs 26:11 says that as a dog returns to its vomit, so a fool repeats his folly. Peter gives the first half in a short form of his own.

decisions.choice: the pig: a saying not found in the Old Testament
decisions.reason: The second saying is not in Scripture. A similar saying about a pig that is bathed and goes back to the mud appears in some versions of the Story of Ahikar, an ancient book of sayings. To Jewish readers dogs and pigs were both unclean animals (compare Matthew 7:6): the people Peter describes were washed and went back to their filth.

decisions.choice: two proverbs in clipped form, with no main verb
decisions.reason: Both sayings use a participle and leave the verb understood, as proverbs often do: "a dog, turned back to its vomit", "a sow, washed, to wallowing in mud". τὸ ("the thing") refers to what the proverb says.

decisions.choice: washed: the pig had been clean
decisions.reason: λουσαμένη is middle, "having washed" or "having had a wash". The point is that the pig had been clean and went back to the dirt, as these people had escaped the world's filth (verse 20) and returned to it.

decisions.choice: goes back
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply the verb the proverbs leave out (m3); Literal keeps the clipped form.
